analysis.summary: The PR introduces high-severity functional bugs including a documentation path conflict that breaks the API contract and missing exports for the Lambda handlers.

bugs.title: OpenAPI Path Conflict
bugs.description: The new getCustomerSEDDoc incorrectly defines its path as '/salesforce/v1/customer', which is identical to the existing getCustomerDoc route. The actual API route defined in the stack is '/salesforce/v1/customer/sed'.
bugs.risk: This causes a collision in the generated OpenAPI/Swagger specification where two GET methods exist for the same path. This will break automated client generation and prevent the new SED endpoint from being correctly documented or discoverable.

bugs.title: Lambda Handler Export and Signature Mismatch
bugs.description: The logic function 'getCustomer' is exported with a new signature (expecting headers and query parameters), while the actual API handlers 'customerHandler' and 'customersHandler' are not exported. Since the API stack refers to 'getCustomer' and 'getCustomers', there is a mismatch between the expected Lambda entry point and the available exports.
bugs.risk: The Lambda function will fail at runtime. If it invokes 'getCustomer' directly, it will receive the Lambda event object instead of the expected header/query data, leading to logic failures. If it tries to invoke the non-exported handlers, the Lambda execution will crash immediately with an export error.

notBugs.reason: Checking event.rawPath to switch between CustomerSEDHeadersSchema and CustomerHeadersSchema is an intentional design to support both authenticated and unauthenticated access within the same Lambda function.
Calling the shared 'getCustomer' logic from both paths is intended, as the feature aims to provide the same data access but with different authentication requirements for SED.
